Incident: Capita plc / Capita Pension Solutions Ltd (UK outsourcer) cyber incident, March 2023 (Black Basta claimed). About 1TB exfiltrated, including data of hundreds of pension-scheme clients, then ransomware
Access path: On 22 Mar 2023 an employee downloaded a malicious JavaScript file, probably a drive-by download with no phishing evidence. Qakbot and Cobalt Strike followed. Kerberos credential harvesting compromised a 'backupadmin' Domain Admin service account. Within about 4h21m the attacker pivoted across eight Capita domains (BloodHound reconnaissance). On 29-30 Mar about 975GB was exfiltrated via Rclone and SystemBC. On 31 Mar ransomware hit at least 1,057 hosts.
Orgs reached (as reported): 325 pension scheme organisations affected out of 600+ client organisations, per the ICO press release, Oct 2025. Data was taken from Capita's own servers; no intrusion into client networks is reported.
Coding notes: [E239] ICO notice, ICO page and RNS texts returned 403 or blank; details via law-firm and Register summaries of ICO notice. Shell=Y for the JavaScript file (T1059.007). Black Basta in media only, not ICO. 'backupadmin' was a credential, not backup disruption. 325 schemes from ICO press release.
People or orgs exposed: 6,656,037 individuals (631,816 where Capita was controller; 6,024,221 where CPSL was processor), across 325 pension scheme organisations. ICO penalty notice and press release, 15 Oct 2025.

Incident: Norwegian Government Security and Service Organisation (DSS) shared ICT platform (Depnet/U) serving 12 ministries breached via Ivanti EPMM (MobileIron Core) zero-days CVE-2023-35078 and CVE-2023-35081, discovered July 2023
Access path: An APT actor exploited the internet-facing Ivanti EPMM mobile device management and email-synchronisation server. CVE-2023-35078 (auth bypass) was used to enumerate users and admins, run LDAP queries against AD and change EPMM configuration. CVE-2023-35081 was suspected for webshell upload and commands. The actor tunnelled through Ivanti Sentry to an internal Exchange server and compromised Depnet/U email servers.
Orgs reached (as reported): 12 ministries on the DSS shared ICT platform (all except the Prime Minister's Office, Defence, Justice and Foreign Affairs). Reported by the Ministry of Local Government and Districts (KDD), DSS and the National Security Authority (NSM) on 24 Jul 2023, and in the DSS annual report 2023. The email servers shared by all 12 were compromised (KDD minister, Storting hearing 12 May 2025). No per-ministry confirmation of data access. AA23-213A says 'several Norwegian organizations'.
Coding notes: [E256] Reach of 12 is the platform's ministry count; no official per-ministry confirmation. Exfiltration never confirmed. Datatilsynet notification is reported only in news. Webshells on Exchange are 'likely', and mi.war on Sentry deleted log entries (T1070). Neither is coded as deployment or security-control change. EPMM configuration changes are unspecified. Two regjeringen.no pages returned 403; their content comes via search snippets.
People or orgs exposed: 12 ministries (staff of the ministries on the DSS platform; no individual count), 24 Jul 2023

Coding notes: [E009] BeyondTrust and Treasury pages returned 403. Their content was checked via WA SOC advisory and search summaries. The 17 count and password resets come from BeyondTrust. The third-party zero-day and Silk Typhoon attribution come from secondary sources. Exfiltration is NR: Treasury says documents were 'accessed', news says 'stole'. Credential access Y refers to the API-key theft. Service disruption is response-induced (instances suspended).
People or orgs exposed: 17 organisations (Remote Support SaaS customers), BeyondTrust advisory, Jan 2025

Incident: SonicWall MySonicWall cloud backup service breach, Sep-Nov 2025
Access path: A state-sponsored actor used an API call to pull firewall configuration backup files from SonicWall's MySonicWall cloud backup environment. Marquis's complaint says a February 2025 API code change let attackers fetch files without authentication by guessing serial numbers. That is an allegation.
Orgs reached (as reported): SonicWall first said under 5% of firewalls (Sep 17, 2025). It later said all customers who had used the cloud backup service (Oct 2025; Mandiant-led investigation finished Nov 4, 2025). It gave no count. Marquis (vendor to 70+ banks and credit unions) alleges it was harmed downstream; SonicWall disputes this.
Coding notes: [E054] Reach band inferred from 'all cloud-backup customers' (no count given). Secrets were encrypted (AES-256 on Gen7, 3DES on Gen6); configs readable. Exfiltration left NR: SonicWall says only 'accessed'. Marquis alleges the stolen configs enabled its Aug 2025 ransomware breach (672,075 people, Maine AG); SonicWall denies evidence of a link. Ransomware not coded. Pre-assigned values kept. Service disruption N->NR at merge (no explicit denial).
People or orgs exposed: All MySonicWall cloud-backup customers, count not disclosed (SonicWall, Oct 2025; confirmed Nov 4, 2025)
